reply:
Rounding on write doesn't fix the calculation—it hides one symptom.

You calculated the total in JavaScript using floats. That calculation was already wrong. Rounding it in the DB on write locks in whichever rounding error happened to occur that time. 

The cost of being wrong: silent financial data corruption. Your invoice total might be off by a cent, but your recorded transaction is now disconnected from the actual math that produced it. If you later retrieve that rounded total and do more calculations (tax, refunds, reconciliation), errors compound from corrupted source data. You lose the single source of truth for what this transaction actually cost.

The fix is where the money is handled: use integer cents (or Decimal) for all invoice calculations in JavaScript, then store the correct value. No rounding needed—you have the true total.

grade.note: Reply reasserts the calculation error is in stored values, explains why rounding-on-write doesn't fix it, and reiterates the integer cents/Decimal fix.
